structured_output.title: Fewer per-tick allocations in car pose; dead code and stale docs
structured_output.summary: groundUnderBody reuses the sim's existing Ground scratch and drops a throwaway array per ramp. groundAt rewrites every field of `out` before returning, and only `.h` is read straight away, so pose numbers are bit-identical. Two small dead bits are deleted: an unused getter and a redundant copy of each prop row in validateTrack. Stale comments are fixed in the sim, the driver roster and CLAUDE.md's race-ui line, and a new test covers inline colour on the pause and results screens. No simulation maths, constants, RNG calls, geometry or CSS change.

chosen.why: Real: car.ts:206 calls groundAt with no `out`, so each sample allocates through the default at track.ts:555, and car.ts:201 builds `[-1e-6, -r.length]` for every ramp. groundAt resets h/gx/gz/ramp before writing, and carViews (world.ts:122) never runs while moveWithCollisions/updateVertical hold `ground`, so reusing the scratch is safe. Push the two t values in the same order (-1e-6, then -r.length) with the same |t| < half check. Same ts order and hs values. Per-tick allocation win, small growth.

Real: track.ts:224 already builds a fresh object per row, and :240 spreads each one again. `fail` returns never, so `side` is already narrowed to 'left'|'right' without `as const`. Return `propRows` directly, as ramps and props are. Same values, deletes code. Must pass typecheck.
Real: `get triangleCount` (geometry.ts:134-137) has no reader. The only other matches are an unrelated journal field in harness/. Deleting it changes no geometry.

Real: car.ts:78 says applying maxStepUp everywhere is fine 'before G3', but replay baselines exist in tests/baselines/replays/. Comment only. It stops a later night from treating a global physics change as acceptable.
Real: types.ts:15 says width is 8.4, but dust-bowl uses 11, and bot.ts:1 calls the bot 'the race opponent' though races now have five. Comment-only fixes with no code change.

Real: drivers.ts:21-22 stacks two doc comments on PLAYER_CAR_COUNT, so raceDrivers has none. Move line 21 above raceDrivers and fix 'an `carCount`' to 'a `carCount`'. Only comments change, and the file is in no open PR.

Real: CLAUDE.md:39 says race-ui produces finish-panel updates, but race-ui.ts imports createResultsScreen and createPauseScreen and never imports finish-panel. Today is Sunday, so CLAUDE.md may be edited. Change only this line, to '…HUD, countdown, pause-screen and results-screen updates.'

Real gap: no-inline-colour.test.ts never builds createPauseScreen, and results-screen.test.ts checks only 4 paint attributes. Add one new test file that renders the pause screen (show({lap:1,laps:3,timeMs:0})) and a createRaceUi synced to a finished RaceView. Apply the full COLOUR_PROPS/COLOUR_VALUE/PAINT_ATTRS checks and allow only url(#…) fills (the hatch). It passes on main: icons use currentColor via CSS, and the only paint attribute is the hatch url fill. Tests only.

rejected.reason: It adds a helper and an import to src/sim to replace five one-line expressions, so src/ grows a little for no performance gain. It also touches hot sim paths for low value. Not worth a night under the delete-only rule for tidy-ups.

Dropping `export` from attachOutline requires editing the re-export in src/render/index.ts. That file is touched by open PR #23 (which is also why C006 is held), and it is the gate-facing render seam. Wait for #23.
The local helper adds about as many lines as it saves (net ≥0) across two call sites. That is cosmetic churn, not a deletion.
A types-only rename with zero net lines. Cosmetic churn.

Grouping the selectors would keep computed styles the same (specificity is unchanged). But it moves results-screen layout into screens.css, coupling two stylesheets for a few lines saved. Low value. Leave it for a night that touches the stripe styles anyway.

It overlaps C013 (chosen) on the race-ui line. Its other edits rewrite the owner's conventions: what registers by folder, and the planned cars/features content layout. Whether to drop or keep those as intent is the owner's call, not an unattended refactor's.

playtest.whatYoullSee: Nothing should look or feel different. Cars sit and pitch on ramps exactly as before, every track loads the same, and the pause and results screens look the same. Apart from one new test, the only changes are an internal allocation fix, deleted dead code and corrected comments.
howToTest: Race Dust Bowl and drive over the ramp: the car tilts up the slope, leaves the lip and lands as before, with no jitter or sinking into the ramp.
Watch the AI cars over the ramps: they tilt and sit on the ground as before.
Race Bramble Bends: hay bales, tyre stacks and trees line the track in the same places as before.
Pause and resume a race: the pause card looks and behaves as before.
Finish a race: the results screen, its stripes and its table look as before, and RETRY and NEXT RACE still work.
